findings.assessment: The first output adds cc-claim-v2 directly to cc-launch-check in chg-cc-launch-check-deps. After the other valid changes, cc-launch-check already receives the v2 result through cc-paid -> cc-landing-copy -> cc-claim-v2 and cc-crm -> cc-email-copy -> cc-claim-v2. Its existing criteria still ask for final channel-version consistency, so it remains a transitive consumer.

findings.title: 其他依赖差分与旧边处理正确

findings.title: 草稿与正式关系冲突证据基本完整
findings.assessment: The output correctly cites the partial v2 draft and the formal dependency conflict together. Preservation of the completed v1 history is also supported by the formal task and history; citing cc-d6 in the reasoning item would make the withdrawn overwrite proposal more explicit, but this is not the cause of the dependency error.

attribution.planner: Responsible for the material error: it converted a transitive consumer into a direct consumer and produced a fifth update that violates minimal-difference planning.
attribution.fixture: The frozen input is sufficient. Although the user says several tasks should consume v2, the existing dependency graph and each task's criteria distinguish direct channel producers from the final consistency check; no fixture repair is required.
attribution.grader: A grader should reject the extra cc-launch-check update. The frozen expectation has three independent protections: mustNotUpdateTaskIds, maxUpdates=4 and exactDependencies. If a grader accepts this output, that is a grader enforcement gap; rejecting it is correct.

attribution.planner: Correct. The first output makes one update, preserves all old direct producers, adds only the three evidenced missing producers and leaves all transitive tasks unchanged.

crossCaseConclusions: A user's statement that several tasks should consume a new result does not automatically make every named task a direct dependency consumer; the existing graph and each task's own result boundary decide direct versus transitive.
A final launch or handover check should not receive a redundant source-task edge when its direct channel or document producers already carry the result and its criteria remain accurate.

Adding a new producer never authorizes deletion of a still-consumed old producer. REAL-C-04 and REAL-A-ECOM-01 correctly retain old edges; REAL-C-01 correctly removes only the explicitly superseded v1 edges but incorrectly adds one redundant downstream edge.
Conflict reasoning is strongest when it cites the informal report or draft and the formal task status or signed evidence in the same reasoning item.
